questions.q: Unlike traditional artists who mostly learned through family apprenticeships, pioneering contemporary Nigerian artists generally acquired their skills through:
options: Formal education in schools, colleges, and universities.
Only imitating European artists without training.
questions.explain: A defining feature of contemporary Nigerian artists is their formal academic training in modern art schools (both in Nigeria and abroad), departing from the traditional guild and family apprenticeship systems.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Nigerian Art Heritage & Pioneers

questions.q: A major group of young contemporary Nigerian artists in the late 1950s broke away from strict Western art traditions to promote 'Natural Synthesis' (blending African heritage with modern techniques). What were they popularly called?
questions.explain: The 'Zaria Rebels' (Zaria Art Society), which included Bruce Onabrakpeya, Uche Okeke, and Demas Nwoko, advocated for 'Natural Synthesis'—combining their Nigerian cultural identity with Western artistic techniques.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Nigerian Art Heritage & Pioneers
questions.subject: Arts

questions.q: Uche Okeke, another pioneering Nigerian contemporary artist, heavily based his modern drawing and painting styles on which traditional indigenous art form?
options: Uli traditional body and wall painting
questions.explain: Uche Okeke pioneered the 'Uli art movement', integrating the linear, lyrical motifs of traditional Igbo 'Uli' body and wall painting into modern canvas paintings and drawings.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Nigerian Art Heritage & Pioneers

questions.q: Which Nigerian contemporary artist is credited with designing the official emblem for the Second World Black and African Festival of Arts and Culture (FESTAC ’77)?
questions.explain: Erhabor Emokpae, a leading modern Nigerian artist and sculptor, designed the iconic FESTAC '77 logo, basing it on the 16th-century Benin ivory mask of Queen Idia.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Nigerian Art Heritage & Pioneers

questions.q: What is the meaning of 'Contemporary Art' in the context of Nigerian art history?
options: Art that was produced before the colonial era using only raw local materials.
Art of the present day, usually created by academically trained artists responding to a globalized, modern society.
Art that is exclusively made for religious shrines.
Art that is dug out from archaeological sites.
questions.explain: Contemporary art refers to modern, present-day art. In Nigeria, it marks the shift from functional traditional shrine arts to individualistic, aesthetically-driven artworks produced by formally trained artists.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Nigerian Art Heritage & Pioneers
questions.subject: Arts

questions.q: Many of Nigeria's pioneering contemporary artists, such as Uche Okeke and Bruce Onabrakpeya, received their formal art training from which historic Nigerian educational institution?
options: The Yaba College of Technology, Lagos
The Nigerian College of Arts, Science and Technology (NCAST), Zaria
questions.explain: The Nigerian College of Arts, Science and Technology in Zaria (now Ahmadu Bello University) was the premier institution where many of the most famous first-generation modern Nigerian artists (the Zaria Rebels) studied.
